William Bligh of Mutiny on the Bounty fame was an excellent naval officer, not the tyrant portrayed in popular fiction.

Though the cause of the mutiny is still debated, he resorted to discipline of the crew less often than was typical of the Royal Navy at the time. IMHO, the mutiny directly resulted from the return to naval discipline after a too languorous period in Tahiti. The crew were unwilling to return to the harsh life of a British Sailor after such a taste of paradise (including much of female companionship). The betrayal of Fletcher Christian is mystifying to this day as he was a close and trusted friend of Bligh's.

Following the mutiny, Bligh navigated a 23' launch across the Pacific, a journey of 3600nm and 47 days at sea. He subsequently had a long and prosperous naval career and retired as the First Lord of the Admiralty (head of the Royal Navy).
